problem: is_empty now uses `or` instead of `and`, so half-open zero-width intervals [a,a) and (a,a] count as non-empty; normalize, intersection and difference then return phantom intervals, e.g. intersection([0,5),[5,10]) = [(5,5,T,F)], difference(A,A) != [], and difference([0,inf),[5,inf)) emits (inf, None, True, False).
The emptiness rule that every operation depends on was changed with no tests; the repo has none, and a single half-open degenerate-interval test would have caught F1.
Pre-existing: is_number accepts float('nan'), so NaN bounds pass validation and make sorting, merging and intersection silently wrong (e.g. normalize([(nan,1)]) returns [(nan,1,True,True)]).
Pre-existing: validate_bounds rejects closed ends only for None, so a closed float('-inf')/float('inf') bound is accepted and exported as a closed None end that the parser itself rejects.
Pre-existing: is_number catches only TypeError, so Decimal('NaN') raises decimal.InvalidOperation instead of the ValueError that parse documents.
